newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss extend detention of Russian "godfather".
newsitem.headline: Swiss extend detention of Russian "godfather".

text.p: A Geneva court has extended the detention of a Russian man jailed seven months ago for suspected links to the Moscow underworld and money-laundering, a Swiss justice official said on Wednesday.

Prosecutor Christian Coquoz told Reuters that police were still investigating the affairs of Sergei Mikhailov, suspected of money laundering and illegal property purchases in Switzerland. "It is a very complicated investigation," he said.
Mikhailov was arrested in October in Geneva, Switzerland's secretive private banking hub for the world's very rich which bankers say is attracting potentially dirty money from Russia.
The 38-year-old Russian -- dubbed "the Godfather" by the Swiss media -- is likely to face trial in Switzerland in the coming months, Coquoz said.
Geneva's bankers are secretive about their Russian clients. Many say they have no Russian exposure, but some statistics put the volume of Russian deposits at Swiss banks at well over $3 billion.

Russians can be seen everywhere in Geneva -- talking business in luxury hotel lobbies and registering with the offices of Geneva's police for foreigners. Drivers can be seen picking up Russian children at Geneva's international school.
Downtown Geneva now has at least one foreign exchange office with Russian signs, next to a big department store whose jewellery stand advertises in Russian: "We sell gold here".
